title: Why 99% Accurate Browser Agents Still Fail — Derek Meegan, Browserbase
talk_summary: Browserbase's Derek Meegan argues that long agent trajectories compound per-step failure (99% per step over 100 steps ≈ 36% end-to-end), so production reliability comes from shrinking the model's decision surface: deterministic tools, reusable auth, verification tools, and SOP-style skills. He also recommends measuring success per transaction with retries rather than per run, and treating cost/maintainability as optimization problems once performance is established.

takeaways.what_they_do: Measure success at the transaction level and allow bounded retries, rather than judging each run in isolation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: permit retries and measure success against a per transaction basis
takeaways.numbers: 50% per-run success with up to 4 retries climbs to 94% per transaction

takeaways.technique: Collapse multi-step operations into one deterministic tool
takeaways.what_they_do: Encapsulate a complex, repeatable browser operation (download + retrieve file) into a single tool call so the model doesn't decide each sub-step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of the model needing to make decisions on the fly, you encapsulate a complex operation into a single tool call.

takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent a tool that deterministically checks its output against a system of record so it knows authoritatively whether it succeeded.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it has a deterministic mechanism to verify that

takeaways.technique: SOP-style skills to constrain the critical path
takeaways.what_they_do: Write a standard-operating-procedure skill that tells the agent the critical path steps, reducing ambiguity in its decision process.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we introduce the critical path to the agent, it knows it's at step two

takeaways.technique: Move invariant logic out of the model
takeaways.what_they_do: Pull never-changing logic (authentication) out of the model's responsibility into reusable deterministic functions shared across workflows.

takeaways.technique: Define success as a concrete artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Specify success for each transactional workflow as a queryable artifact (receipt, order ID, new record) rather than a subjective judgment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: success in these transactional browser trajectories look like some kind of concrete artifact that the run leaves behind
